statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Overnight follow-through is limited relative to Tuesday’s technology selloff, and persistent one-way NQ structure is not independently verified.
recommendation: Mapped policy state remains WATCH. Tail is below the block threshold; the FOMC minutes are the principal conditional risk checkpoint in the next 24 hours.
headline: Overnight follow-through eases; FOMC remains the key second-leg risk
body: Tuesday’s Nasdaq decline and semiconductor rout left a clear downside backdrop, but fresh supplementary delayed futures context shows only mild overnight NQ weakness rather than renewed broad extension. Oil, long-end yields and Strait of Hormuz disruption keep Stress extreme. The July FOMC minutes create the strongest conditional delayed-repricing window later today.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 hours, Tail rose from low/watch levels to a 32% peak during Tuesday’s technology-led selloff, then eased to 26% by 23:00 UTC as late-session mean reversion appeared.
outlookSummary: The overnight state is WATCH rather than block. Conditional risk rises around the U.S. cash session and EIA release, and most sharply around the 18:00 UTC FOMC minutes and possible delayed rates-to-equity second leg.

forecast.analysis: Tuesday’s tech-led selloff remains the main backdrop, but fresh delayed futures context shows only mild overnight downside and no verified repeated extension. Tail is therefore WATCH rather than block; oil, yields and Hormuz keep Stress extreme.
drivers: Delayed overnight futures show limited follow-through

news.title: Tech selloff weighs down Wall Street as bond yields climb
Trump says no talks planned with Iran, Tehran says Strait of Hormuz still shut

forecast.analysis: Overnight follow-through is conditional. A deeper one-way decline would require fresh confirmation from NQ structure; absent that, modest stabilization after Tuesday’s selloff allows Tail to ease while headline Stress stays extreme.

Asia-session risk remains conditional on whether technology weakness broadens again. Without observed failed retracements, the forecast trims Tail while retaining high Stress from elevated yields, oil and geopolitical uncertainty.

During the quieter overnight window, the key test is whether NQ can hold a two-sided profile. Continued retracements would argue against a kill path; renewed extension with no pullback would invalidate this easing profile.

Pre-European trading remains vulnerable to headline shocks, but no scheduled U.S. catalyst is due in this hour. Tail stays in WATCH territory unless new price-path evidence confirms persistent downside efficiency.
drivers: Persistent downside structure not yet verified

forecast.analysis: European pre-open risk is mainly transmission from Tuesday’s technology selloff and the rates/oil backdrop. In the absence of fresh NQ extension, Tail continues to edge lower conditionally.

Early Europe can test whether global technology weakness broadens across regions. The forecast keeps Stress high, but Tail remains sub-block unless NQ develops shallow pullbacks and repeated downside extension.

European cash trading can reintroduce cross-asset pressure through yields and oil. Tail lifts slightly because broader confirmation could reappear, though any move remains conditional until current NQ structure verifies it.

Europe-to-U.S. handoff risk rises modestly. Persistent weakness in semiconductors, yields and oil would increase directional pressure, while meaningful retracements would keep Tail below the blocking threshold.
Mid-European session remains a monitoring hour rather than an automatic danger window. The key condition is whether cross-asset downside alignment persists into U.S. premarket liquidity.

Approaching U.S. premarket, event proximity raises Stress more than Tail. Without observed one-way NQ structure, the forecast allows a small Tail easing before the U.S. session becomes the main price-discovery venue.
drivers: Observed path remains decisive for Tail

forecast.analysis: Late European trading is a transition hour. If NQ remains two-sided, Tail stays below block; renewed semiconductor-led downside with firmer yields and oil would raise continuation risk into U.S. premarket.

U.S. premarket liquidity begins to matter more. Existing tech weakness and elevated yields can amplify downside, but the forecast still requires actual failed retracements before Tail can cross the block threshold.

The U.S. cash open is the first major price-path checkpoint. Opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would raise Tail; orderly two-sided discovery would keep the state in WATCH despite very high Stress.

The EIA petroleum release at 14:30 UTC can affect oil, inflation expectations and yields. Tail is WATCH because a stronger one-way Nasdaq path is conditional on the release transmitting into persistent cross-asset alignment.

Post-EIA and early cash-session trading should reveal whether the rates/oil channel is reinforcing technology weakness. Tail remains below block unless NQ repeatedly extends after failed retracements.

Mid-session risk can ease if the opening move retraces and cross-assets stabilize. Without that stabilization, lingering trend pressure would keep Tail elevated but still conditional ahead of the Fed minutes.

The hour before the FOMC minutes carries event/whipsaw risk. Tail rises modestly on the existing rates-sensitive backdrop, but the scheduled release alone does not count as observed one-way structure.

The FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC create the day’s main conditional Tail window. A rates-driven first move followed by failed retracements or a delayed second leg would justify the elevated forecast; an orderly reaction would not.

The first post-minutes hour carries the highest delayed-repricing risk. Tail remains elevated only if yields, semiconductors and NQ stay directionally aligned and retracements fail after the initial interpretation.

Late post-FOMC trading can still produce a second equity leg after bond-market interpretation. Tail stays elevated conditionally, but would fall quickly if price discovery becomes two-sided and volatility decays.

CME’s daily maintenance interval removes live futures price discovery. Tail drops to WATCH mechanically for observed-path evidence, while unresolved FOMC interpretation and geopolitical Stress remain relevant for the reopening.

Futures reopening after maintenance is a second-leg checkpoint. Tail returns above block only conditionally if the post-FOMC direction resumes with shallow retracements and aligned yields/technology weakness.

The final forecast hour retains modest elevated Tail because a delayed FOMC second leg can persist overnight. Failure to extend, improving breadth and calmer cross-assets would support a rapid return below the block threshold.
